title: Russell rues ‘misjudgement’ that cost him Sao Paulo pole
excerpt:
A bittersweet Qualifying in Sao Paulo left George Russell feeling frustrated after a “misjudgement” cut his lap that “would’ve been good enough for pole” short, but his performance still gave him “confidence” for Sunday’s Grand Prix.

Nearly a week after he lost out on the Drivers’ Championship to his team mate Kimi Antonelli, Russell bounced back to fight for the top spot in Qualifying at Interlagos – a challenge that was made particularly difficult by torrential rain.

Despite the conditions, he mingled around the P1 slot on the timesheets before the weather worsened after the first Q3 runs. Assuming they’d get the chance to complete another lap, Mercedes told Russell to back off with Alex Albon just ahead, which proved to be the wrong call as his effort to that point was faster than polesitter Lando Norris’.

Elaborating on his subsequent flurry of irritated radio messages, he said: “Pole was ours for the taking there. It was just a misjudgement from us collectively as a team to abort my second lap.

“We thought we’d get another 60s without the rain – unfortunately, we got that wrong. That was a pole lap, I think. I got a bit held up by Albon, but it still would’ve been good enough for the pole.

“[The race is] going to be tricky, but it gives me confidence. It reminds me again that I’ve not forgotten how to drive, and I think that’s important in circumstances like these that I found myself in.

“It would’ve meant a lot to me to have clinched the pole with a great performance, like we showed in Qualifying. I think it kind of sums up this season.

“As a team, we’ve got one goal this weekend and that’s to seal the Constructors’. This season’s just very much not meant to be.”

Although Russell’s five-place grid penalty will demote him to P7, Mercedes will still be on course to score the three extra points they need to beat Ferrari to the Teams’ Championship, especially with Antonelli starting on the front row.

The Italian didn’t look as confident as Russell throughout Qualifying and wound up 0.625s adrift of Norris’ time, but moving up to P2 on the grid will put him in a strong position to add a 10th Grand Prix win to his tally.

“[It was] very difficult trying to understand this track in the wet,” Antonelli admitted. “It was [my] first time around here in the wet, and it just was not easy.

“Very slippery but I think in Q3 there was a lot more. I just made two big mistakes during the lap and that cost us the chance for a better position.

“I’m looking forward to [the race] if it’s wet. Obviously I have a lot more experience now with the car, so if it’s wet it’s going to be fun, but if it’s dry we’re going to do our best. I think overall there’s been big learning this session. Not how I wanted it to go, but still decent.”

title: What To Watch For in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos
excerpt:
From Mercedes on the verge of another title to Max Verstappen chasing a hat-trick of recovery drives through the field, and from Ferrari also needing to recover from grid penalties to a new home hero chasing points on debut, here are just some of the areas you might want to keep an eye out for as we prepare for what is often an action-packed race at Interlagos.

1. Mercedes’ championship requirements

After Kimi Antonelli won the Drivers’ Championship last week in Mexico City, Mercedes can follow suit and secure the Constructors’ Championship themselves on Sunday.

The equation is a simple one: Mercedes need to outscore Ferrari by three points in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix to become champions, and they have a huge chance to do so given the grid penalties that both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc are taking this weekend.

title: Hamilton reflects on grid penalties and PU changes in Brazil
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton admits that he was "using the Qualifying session as a test", with the Ferrari driver set to start at the back of the grid for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

The seven-time World Champion started Saturday in Brazil with a 10-place grid penalty, along with team mate Charles Leclerc, after both their cars had an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) change.

But Hamilton suffered problems during Free Practice 3, with Ferrari forced to change more power unit elements ahead of Qualifying which resulted in further grid penalties.

Hamilton went out in the second part of a wet Qualifying, admitting that there was a lack of running in order to save tyres for a potentially wet 71-lap race on Sunday.

"It was a lot of fun out there. It's always fun in the rain. It's very, very tricky, but I had just a lot of fun, just in the few laps that we got," said Hamilton.

"I wish I was still out there battling with the guys, but unfortunately, saving the tyres for tomorrow."

"That's what we're trying to do, yeah," said Hamilton when asked if a charge through the field from P20 was possible.

"It's going to be really tricky conditions, but I love racing in the rain. I was basically using the Qualifying session as a test in making sure the engine is working and making sure that the car felt good, so I feel good for tomorrow."

Leclerc managed to reach the final part of Qualifying and finished fourth fastest, which will be converted to a P14 start after his penalty is applied.

Having claimed to have "learnt a huge amount today" during the wet weather running, the Monegasque driver was hopeful of reaching the podium with a climb through the field.

"I'm feeling good, I'm looking forward to it," said Leclerc. "We knew taking an engine penalty here, we knew that everything is to play for still because you've got crazy weather all the time.

"It's good to see that the weather is still crazy for tomorrow and hopefully that will give us an opportunity to come back on the podium from where we start."

title: 'All to play for' in Sao Paulo after Qualifying – Hulkenberg
excerpt:
Nico Hulkenberg believes there is "all to play for" in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with the Audi driver set to start Sunday's race from fourth on the grid.

The German was one of the star drivers during a wet Qualifying session at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, with proceedings initially delayed after heavy rain hit the circuit.

Once running took place, Hulkenberg featured towards the top of the leaderboard, eventually taking the fifth-fastest time in the first two segments of Qualifying, before finishing P6 overall.

Hulkenberg, who took his only Formula 1 pole position at the track in 2010 – also in a rain-affected session – will start two spots higher due to grid penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

The result was Hulkenberg and Audi's best of the season and comes after the one-time podium finisher failed to complete any running on Friday after technical issues with his car.

"Typical, classic Sao Paulo I guess. You never know when the shower is going to hit you and how hard it is," said Hulkenberg.

"But very happy obviously after yesterday, good recovery and I guess the rain helped a bit as well to make up for that lack of running yesterday. But I was happy, confident with the car, managed to produce good laps and yeah, feels nice, feels good."

"We have to see," he said when asked about what was achievable in the race. "All to play for obviously, we're starting in a good position, try to race clean and get the maximum out of it tomorrow."

Team mate Gabriel Bortoleto was unable to join Hulkenberg in Q3 after the Brazilian crashed out in the opening segment of Qualifying.

The home hero ran off the track at Turn 12 at the bottom of the hill, skating across the wet grass and into the tyre barrier.

Although able to recover back to the pits, the damage sustained to his car meant he was unable to continue, leaving him "very disappointed with myself".

"[It] was tough. I messed up, was early in the Qualifying, I locked up a bit, went straight in the grass and I couldn't stop the car in time before hitting the wall," said Bortoleto.

"Obviously then I had rear wing issues, or damage, and I couldn't continue."

title: What the teams said – Qualifying in Brazil
excerpt:
McLaren

Norris is a wet weather master, and as soon as the rain fell, he came right into the reckoning for pole. He kept his Qualifying clean, pumping in fast lap after fast lap and nailed his final effort before the rain got heavier to grab pole. It was a strong effort from him, and he will be hoping for more rain tomorrow – in the dry, Antonelli in P2 could be more of a handful for the McLaren man to deal with. As for Piastri, he was unable to complete his last lap in Q2 due to red flags, missing out on the opportunity to try and progress.

Lando Norris, 1st, 1:27.470

“It was a very tricky Qualifying session, with conditions changing all the time. The priority was to stay calm, understand how the tyres and car were coming up to temperature, and avoid mistakes. I felt confident in the wet from Q1, and I’m pleased we put the lap together when it mattered. This is a track I enjoy, but we know we have not had the pace of Mercedes in the dry, and today the car has not felt quite as strong as it did earlier on in the weekend.

"A big thank you to the team for continuing to work hard and giving me the opportunity to fight for Pole. Today it felt like we had more pace in the wet and on Intermediates. The conditions could make it a challenging race with a bit of everything, so we’ll need to stay focused and make the most of our chances."

Oscar Piastri, 12th, 1:30.369

"Today’s Qualifying was a very tough session, especially at the beginning, when the track was incredibly slippery. It became a little easier towards the end, but the call on tyres was always going to be difficult because I was a long way up the road and there was always a risk that an earlier Red Flag could change things, but we paid the price by missing out on Q3.

"The car felt reasonable in the wet, and we’ve been more competitive and comfortable in the dry this weekend, so it’s disappointing not to have made more of the session. We’ll review what happened and see what the weather and final grid order bring tomorrow. If it’s dry, we look strong; if it’s wet, we’re still decent, but we’ll need to work hard overnight and into the race to make progress up the field."

Andrea Stella, Team Principal

"This Pole Position is a real source of satisfaction. Congratulations to Lando, who, in very difficult conditions, put in an excellent lap at the decisive moment at the start of Q3. The whole team did a good job of managing a very tricky session due to the rapidly changing weather conditions. It’s a shame about Oscar, who was let down by a Red Flag just as he was about to complete a lap that would probably have seen him make the cut in Q2. It was difficult to judge the right moment to switch to Intermediate tyres, and the Red Flag was beyond our control.

“We’ve made a significant effort to bring a package of updates here to Brazil and, from what we’ve seen in the three Free Practice sessions, they’re delivering the performance boost we expected. We’ve made progress, although that doesn’t mean we suddenly have the fastest car.

"Tomorrow’s race will be wide open, with a starting grid very different from the usual one due to the combination of a wet Qualifying session and various penalties. The weather conditions will play a decisive role, and it will be vital not to make any mistakes and to react correctly to whatever happens on the track. Today’s result gives us great motivation to tackle this new challenge: we’ll do everything we can to score valuable points for the championship."

Mercedes

Russell often goes well in the wet, and he was regularly popping into the top spot throughout all three segments of Qualifying. Come Q3 when the inters went on, he grabbed provisional pole on the first round of laps, but then Norris went faster. Russell aborted his second timed run after picking up traffic – and then as the rain intensified, he realised his chance had gone. That left the Briton very frustrated, but with a grid penalty, he starts seventh anyway.

As for the new World Champion, he was in the mix up front but could not quite match his team mate in the wet. But thanks to Russell’s penalty, Antonelli will start from second tomorrow.

Kimi Antonelli, 3rd, 1:28.095

"That was a tricky qualifying session but also good fun. It was my first wet qualifying in Formula One, so I was learning a lot and trying to understand the grip and the lines as the conditions changed. I was probably a little too cautious at times and then made two big mistakes on my final lap in Q3, which was a shame as there was definitely more performance there.

"Starting P2 tomorrow still puts us in a really good position though. I’ve felt very good with the car all weekend, particularly in the dry, and I learned a lot today that will help if we have similar conditions in the race. Whether it is wet or dry, I think we have a good chance, and we’ll be going for the win. We want to clinch the Constructors’ Championship and hopefully we can do so with a strong team result."

George Russell, 2nd, 1:27.674

"Obviously I’m disappointed with how qualifying ended today. We definitely had the pace to take pole position, and in a tricky situation we weren’t able to achieve that. Given the circumstances of last weekend, it would have meant a lot to take pole here. We missed pole by nine milliseconds last week when we didn’t really expect to be in that position, whereas today the car felt strong and I felt like I was putting together laps that were capable of being right at the front.

"We collectively made a misjudgement at the end and that’s frustrating, but these things happen. As a driver, you feel that disappointment very strongly in the moment, but it’s important that we stick together and keep the morale high. There were still plenty of positives in our performance today and, in the bigger picture, it doesn’t change a huge amount. We’ll start P7 tomorrow and we’ve still got a great opportunity to move forward, score some strong points for the team, and hopefully clinch the Constructors’ Championship."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"Those were very difficult conditions today and you must take your hat off to the drivers for their collective skill in such treacherous weather. Interlagos can change very quickly, and we saw that throughout the session.

"George had the pace to be on pole today and it is disappointing that he didn’t get the opportunity to finish the job. The call to abort the second lap at the end of Q3 was a real 50-50 decision. He was very slightly up on Norris at that point but was catching Albon and we thought was about to lose time. Without a crystal ball, it was very difficult to know whether to back off and create the space or keep going. In hindsight, with the rain coming on the next lap, we should have kept going but it is very easy to say this after the event. What was most pleasing is that George was very strong throughout and deserved pole position, even if he didn’t get it today.

"Kimi meanwhile did a solid job too in challenging conditions and will start P2 tomorrow. With George’s penalty, we know he has some work to do from further back in P7, but the pace in the car was clear today. We need to execute properly tomorrow and maximise the opportunities we have. With Ferrari starting further back in the field, we know we have an opportunity to clinch the Constructors’ Championship here, but we must focus on deliveringand making the correct decisions."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"We made several small changes to the cars overnight and FP3 gave us a useful opportunity to assess those on the hottest track of the weekend so far. We finished P2 and P4 without either driver feeling they had put together a particularly good lap, so we were optimistic that, had qualifying remained dry, that we would have been fighting at the front.

"The rain arrived at the end of FP3 and continued through to qualifying. Conditions were very poor initially and it was right to red flag the session when the heavier rain arrived. Credit to the FIA too for timing the restart well and allowing us to complete the session in sensible conditions before the light deteriorated further.

"We had decent pace on both the extreme Wet and Intermediate tyres, although the balance wasn’t particularly easy for the drivers. The rear was quite weak and that made it difficult to build confidence. We had a close shave with Kimi in Q2 after leaving the switch to Intermediates a lap later than we should have, but ultimately P2 and P4 on the road is a reasonable team result in such tricky conditions.

"George was understandably frustrated not to get the opportunity to challenge Norris for pole. It was a difficult call at the end of his lap, with Albon ahead, as to whether to back off and create space or continue and risk compromising both that lap and the next. Ultimately, the rain intensified and there was no opportunity to improve.

"We’ve still put ourselves in a good position for tomorrow. We’re expecting more rain and that usually means an eventful race here. We’ve got two cars with good pace and, if we execute well, there should be plenty of opportunity to move forward and fight for the podium."

Ferrari

Both Ferrari cars took on a new ICE in Sao Paulo, meaning both Leclerc and Hamilton were set for 10-place grid drops. But then Hamilton’s car started smoking in FP3, leading to the team swapping in another new engine. That meant a back of the grid start for the British driver.

He took part in Qualifying anyway, looking to learn more about the cars in the wet and was having fun, but could not get his final lap in during Q2 due to red flags. Leclerc did make the top 10 shoot-out, winding up fourth which means a P14 start tomorrow.

Lewis Hamilton, 11th, 1:30.001

"It was fun to drive in the rain today and the car felt good, especially in Q1. I always enjoy these conditions and it felt great to be out there having some close battles. It’s a shame for the penalty because I think we had a car that could have fought further up the order, but tomorrow is a new day and today the team did plenty of work getting me to the track in qualifying after what happened in FP3. Starting from the back tomorrow will make things difficult, but hopefully we’ll have similar conditions and plenty of opportunities. We’ll make sure everything is in the right place with the car and I’ll give it everything to make my way forward, do the best job I can for the team and enjoy the race."

Charles Leclerc, 4th, 1:28.289

"It was a really interesting qualifying for us, even if we are not fully satisfied with the position we finished in. Knowing that we would take a 10-place grid penalty, we were willing to be more experimental and try various things with the car in these conditions. We learned a huge amount today, and I think these learnings will be something to capitalise on tomorrow and take with us going forward.

"Starting from P14, we will do everything to fight our way forward, and with rain predicted, let’s see what’s in the cards for us in a hopefully exciting race."

Fred Vasseur, Team Principal

"It was a very long qualifying session, but I think the Race Director handled it in the right way, as at times the conditions were truly extreme. The positive aspect on our side is that we were competitive in the wet from the very start.

"We knew we would have to take a penalty before the end of the season and, also taking the weather forecast into account, we decided to take it here with both drivers, because Interlagos is a track where we believe it is possible to move up the order. Therefore, so far, we have approached the weekend with the race very much in mind, including in terms of tyre management.

"Tomorrow will certainly be a challenge, but there will also be plenty of opportunities, particularly if the weather remains unpredictable, which looks likely. We have seen in the past that it is possible to make up a lot of places here when starting from the back. We will have to be ready to seize every opportunity."

Racing Bulls

With both Racing Bulls cars in the top 10 in practice, they looked on for another strong Saturday. But in Q2, disaster befell Lindblad, when he was told to park up with an issue. He managed to pull off behind some barriers, thus negating the need for any yellow or red flags which was clever thinking. Lawson though made the top 10 for the team, and grabbed a brilliant P5. That becomes third on the grid when penalties are applied, and gives the Kiwi racer a huge chance of a decent result at a time when he is fighting for his F1 seat.

Liam Lawson, 5th, 1:28.321

"It's been a really good day for us. I had a very strong car throughout Qualifying, which is a big positive for the team. I had to back off on my final push lap because I was too close to Alonso, which was a shame as I think there was potentially more time to find. I’m really happy to be starting P3 in a strong position to make the most of the opportunities in tomorrow’s race. I wouldn’t mind seeing some rain tomorrow, but we know we have a quick car in both conditions, so I’m looking forward to it either way."

Arvid Lindblad, 14th, 1:31.687

"It's a shame to end Qualifying this way. Unfortunately, I had to stop the car due to an issue with the Power Unit, which we'll investigate with the team later on tonight. Since the beginning of Q1, I've been feeling really good and thoroughly enjoying being in the car. I believe there would've been more to come had I been able to continue building through Q2 and Q3. Although I'd already had some experience running in wet weather in Malaysia and Singapore, I think this was my first time really pushing the car to its limits in these conditions. It's important to focus on the fact we're competitive, the car is fast, and Liam and the team have done a great job today. Let's see what tomorrow brings, but I'm confident that if we have a clean race, we can make up some ground and fight for points."

Tim Goss, Chief Technical Officer

"Overall, it's been an amazing wet Qualifying session for the team today, but of course we have mixed emotions. Following Friday's Practice Sessions, we thought we were competitive, but felt there was a little more to come from the car. We now understand our Austin GP aerodynamic upgrade a little better and managed to extract another small step in performance from it, committing to the change for today. Car balance still needed improving in Sector 2, and we managed to address this and make improvements with setup changes over night. In FP3, we showed this had all come together, and we were pleased with our competitiveness in the dry.

"Qualifying was expected to be wet, and after some heavy downpours, the sessions started with the use of the full wet tyre, moving towards the intermediate tyres as the heavy rain held off. The whole package of the car, Power Unit and drivers were exceptional. We knew that if we kept everything clean, avoided mistakes and were on the right tyre at the right time, we would be able to progress through the early stages. As it turned out, we were comfortably quick all the way through Qualifying. Unfortunately, Arvid's Q2 session was curtailed with a mechanical failure. Without this, he looked to be on course to make the Q3 cut-off and a top ten start. We will have a solution for Sunday and are still confident of a successful race. Liam showed his undoubted skill in the wet, and was somewhat frustrated not to get even more out of the car after encountering traffic on his final lap in Q3. It was an impressive session in tricky conditions. His reward is a start on the second row in P3. The race is likely to be wet, and following today's performance we feel we're in a strong position for a points finish."

Audi

It was a mixed bag for Audi on Saturday. Bortoleto looked quick in FP3, but the Brazilian was one of the first to crash in Q1 in treacherous conditions down at Turn 12. He slid over the grass and hit the barriers, damaging his rear wing. Although he managed to make it back to the pits, the damage was too severe to get him back out. Hulkenberg though used all his experience to keep the car on track, making it all the way to Q3. He grabbed sixth, which becomes a very positive P4 for the Grand Prix.

Nico Hulkenberg, 6th, 1:28.668

“Going into qualifying, I just wanted to give it my best shot. I've raced here quite a few times, so I know the circuit well, although missing yesterday's running was obviously not ideal. The key was to keep it clean in very tricky conditions. We had a good session this morning and I felt confident straight away during qualifying, both on the full wets and the intermediates, which allowed me to put together some good laps.

“There is still a big job ahead of us: it's not going to be easy, especially with a wet race expected tomorrow. We'll need to stay sharp, remain focused and aim to bring home the best possible result.”

Gabriel Bortoleto, 22nd, 1:41.564

“It’s been a tough qualifying for me, and obviously not the way I wanted it to go. I locked up early on at turn 12, went straight into the grass and could not stop the car from hitting the wall. Unfortunately, that resulted in rear wing damage and, eventually, and end to my session. Still, I want to thank my mechanics for having tried to repair my car in time to get back to track. Tomorrow is another day, so I want to clear my head and focus on making the most of the race.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director

“First of all, my heart goes out to Gabi, who had been so quick throughout the weekend. Conditions were extremely difficult in qualifying, and unfortunately he made a small mistake, which was enough to bring his session to an end. However, knowing his strength of character, I am sure he will be fighting back tomorrow.

“On the other side of the garage, Nico delivered another fantastic performance. His team gave him a great car, and he once again demonstrated his pace in the wet, showing why he is the Regenmeister, the rain master. Qualifying sixth overall and moving up to fourth on the grid following penalties for other drivers is a well-deserved reward for him and the team. “Overall, it is our best qualifying performance to date, and we are very much looking forward to tomorrow’s race.”

Red Bull

Verstappen was always starting from the back after taking on a raft of new PU components, so he took part in Q1 and then did not come back out, choosing to save wet tyres for tomorrow in case they are needed. But the Dutchman looked strong in the wet and in the dry FP3 session, so he will be one to watch from the back.

Hadjar was complaining on the radio in final practice, calling his car “undriveable” at one point. In the rain he kept his car on track and grabbed seventh, which becomes P5 when grid penalties are applied.

Max Verstappen, 16th, No time set in Q2

“We knew coming into today that Qualifying would be a little different for us given the grid penalty. Nevertheless, FP3 and Qualifying gave us a better understanding of the car and how to get it into the best possible window for tomorrow. Q1 went well and we were competitive, but with the amount of standing water on track and knowing we would be starting from the back, there was no reason to take unnecessary risks.

"Tomorrow will be a challenge. With overtake mode rather than DRS this year, making our way through the field might not be as straightforward as in previous seasons. But I’ll do everything I can to move forward and score as many points as possible. We’ve come through difficult situations before, so let’s see what we can do.”

Isack Hadjar, 7th, 1:28.763

“We took a slightly cautious approach in Q1, but made it through comfortably and showed strong pace in Q2, where we were third fastest. I felt confident going into Q3 and believed we had a real opportunity to fight for a top-three position. We decided to go out towards the end of the session, but the rain got heavier and the track conditions became increasingly difficult. Being one of the last cars on track ultimately worked against us, as there was very little grip and much more aquaplaning than we had anticipated.

"It feels like a missed opportunity because the pace was there, but the car is still competitive and P5 gives us a solid starting position for tomorrow. Hopefully the conditions allow us to race, and we’ll do everything we can to fight for a podium finish.”

Laurent Mekies, Team Principal

“It’s been a busy day here in São Paulo, with plenty of work going on behind the scenes. The Team made a number of changes overnight, and Max’s performance in FP3 was an encouraging indication of the progress we had made. With the power unit change and the resulting grid penalty, we knew Qualifying would require a different approach for Max, particularly in the wet conditions. The focus was on learning as much as possible about the car while avoiding unnecessary risks in those tricky conditions.

"Isack secured P5 on the grid after the various penalties were applied, which gives him a solid starting position for tomorrow, although we know he was hoping for a little more after a very strong Q2. There is still work to do, but we now have a clearer understanding of where we stand and where we need to improve.

"Tomorrow will be a challenging race, particularly for Max starting from the back, but we know how unpredictable racing in Brazil can be. We will stay focused on ourselves, make the most of every opportunity and give both Max and Isack the best possible chance to move forward.”

Haas

Camara faced an incredibly tough ask to compete in his first Qualifying in such wet conditions. He span off early on and hit the barriers, damaging his front wing but the Brazilian kept his composure, made it back to the pits and came back out. He set a good enough time to make Q2, but towards the end of the session he missed his braking point, locking up and going straight on across the grass and into the barriers. However, with so many grid penalties, he will start 11th.

Bearman also went off at one point, but he recovered to make the top 10, and inherits P6. From there, he will be hoping for a big haul of points as he keeps an eye on rival Hulkenberg ahead – Haas and Audi fighting for seventh in the standings.

Oliver Bearman, 8th, 1:29.831

“It was certainly a crazy session. I learned a lot from my first rodeo here two years ago, and I, as well as the team, did a much better job this time around on the wet tyre, when to push and when to cool. We did well, and it’s a shame about Q3 as compared to our competitors, we just struggled to put the tyres in the correct window, so I didn’t have any grip, and then it was game over. I’m happy with the job that we did, there’s a bit more out there, but it’s okay, as we’ll get them tomorrow. I’m looking forward to it, getting a bit more rhythm in the rain, and we had good pace last time out in the wet – so hopefully that comes back and we can do our very best tomorrow.”

Rafael Camara, 13th, 1:31.515

“It was a tricky one, but I’m okay. I was just a bit unlucky in the last corner, locking up, and then trying to make the corner, but it was really not possible. In a way, I’m a bit disappointed with the mistakes, as I know for the team, that’s not what they want, but overall I think it was a positive session. I think one thing we do know, we don’t want to crash tomorrow, and we just try to have a clean race, but I think we’ll go into the data, go into procedures with the team tonight and see what we can do best for tomorrow, and prepare for all the scenarios. There’s a lot to do in the race, but we need to get as ready as we can for a good race.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“Performance-wise, I think it was a positive day. In FP3, we struggled a bit with the hotter track temperature, and we’ve seen it before, our operating window of our car is not really wide enough. In qualifying, from the get-go, it was very challenging conditions, but operationally, the team did a really good job. To do that, I think we’ve improved quite a lot, if you think about what happened in Malaysia, then we made a good step in Singapore, and here today, I’m really proud of the team. Ollie getting into Q3 is nothing short of what everyone in this team deserves. The last time we did that was in China, and he did a fantastic job. Ollie had these conditions two years ago, and he learned a harsh lesson, but he put every learning into it today and judged everything very well, P8 was a very good result.

“Rafa, as a rookie going into his home race, going straight into qualifying was extremely challenging with lots of standing water in Q1. He aquaplaned and got caught out there, but did a very good job to get out of Q1, that was brilliant. In Q2, he was very fast, maybe too fast, but again, they’re extreme conditions to put a rookie in the car. We’ve got to support him and reset, but today he showed how fast he is. In FP3, Q1, and Q2, until he had that moment, he showed exactly why we signed him for next year. On Sunday I believe both drivers can race really well together.”

Aston Martin

Stroll was another to slide off in Q1, and thus exited at the first time of asking. Alonso made it to Q2, and was the first to switch to the inters. It proved a good move, as he made it to Q3 for the first time this season. In the end he wound up ninth, despite coming out first and thus getting the best of the track conditions. It was a strong result for the veteran, who will be another hoping for more rain tomorrow.

Fernando Alonso, 9th, 1:30.311

“We took some risks in today’s Qualifying and secured our first Q3 of the season, so obviously I’m pleased with that. I went into Q3 quite hopeful, but then it rained more and we couldn't get the temperature into the tyres we needed. I don’t think we could have achieved a higher position in the end, but we made the most of our opportunities today and it's a strong result. Let’s see what we can do tomorrow as it’s expected to rain again.”

Lance Stroll, 19th, 1:33.653

“Tricky conditions out there today, but I enjoyed Qualifying. The car felt good and it was fun to go out there in the rain. I’m happy with my last push lap, and considering our recent performance, P19 is a slightly better result for us. There’s more rain expected for tomorrow so it could get interesting and hopefully give us a chance to move forward.”

Mike Krack, Chief Trackside Officer

“Our first Q3 of the season, so that is a positive to take from today. We knew with the changing weather that tyre choice was going to be crucial, and the decision to put Fernando out on the Intermediate in Q2 was a good call. More rain is expected tomorrow, and we will go into the race ready to take advantage of any opportunities that come our way.”

Williams

Sainz also slid off in Q1 at Turn 12, but kept out of the barriers. He went off in the same place in Q2, which left him without a chance to improve when the red flags then came out. Albon made it all the way to Q3 for the first time this year. He wound up 10th, but starts from ninth in a rare positive for a team that is having a difficult season.

Alex Albon, 10th, 1:30.456

“I’m really happy with that result, and it’s great to be back in Q3. It was a difficult session overall, but we extracted the maximum from it. I’m pleased with my laps in Q1 and Q2, which were right on the limit, and the pace felt good again in Q3. The conditions were tough for everyone out there, but honestly, I enjoyed it. We usually go well in these conditions, and we needed the rain today. It’s been a great effort from everyone in the team, so that should give us confidence going into tomorrow. We have been strong on starts, so the plan is to keep it clean and race from there. Points are the target, so let’s hope it stays wet.”

Carlos Sainz, 15th, 1:31.785

“A tricky qualifying out there but the car was feeling really good. We were strong on the extreme wets as we got the tyres working and we were setting competitive lap times. Unfortunately I switched to the intermediate compound one lap too late and the red flag didn’t allow me to put a lap time on the board with that tyre, which was very frustrating but we were just unlucky. The FIA handled today well and made the right call to pause Q1, and they did well to make the most of the gap between showers. A bit of rain tomorrow would be welcome, and if we’re able to stay out of trouble, we can have an exciting race.”

James Vowles, Team Principal

“A really great effort from the whole team. It was fantastic to be here and listen to how the team was organising themselves: getting the tyres ready, making the call to go to inters, and using all the modes.

"With Alex, some of the trickiest conditions I can remember, and he delivered when it mattered most. Particularly for me, his Q2 lap and the real stress on that inter, it was a brilliant job. Carlos was on a good lap but, unfortunately, got caught in the red flag from Câmara, but I’m sure he’ll be up there tomorrow with the rest.

"Delaying the session was the right decision, so well done to F1 and the FIA on delivering a great qualifying in difficult circumstances. It looks like tomorrow we may have more of the same rain, and I look forward to it.”

Alpine

Gasly tends to go well in the wet, so it was some surprise to see him struggle at the start of Qualifying. His team mate was also up against it, with Alpine looking like they were not able to get heat into their tyres in the difficult conditions. In the end, both drivers exited in Q1 in a disappointing display. They do at least inherit a couple of places, with Verstappen and Hamilton dropping to the back.

Pierre Gasly, 18th, 1:33.449

“We were just too slow today and it's a frustrating end to our day. When it rains, usually opportunities come your way and I've had good memories in the past here in the wet conditions, so to be out in Q1 is of course very disappointing. We just lacked pace the whole session which, to me, is very odd. We struggled for pace compared to everyone else so we need to quickly look into why and hopefully improve for tomorrow where the conditions could be very similar to today. It will be a challenge from that far back but we'll review everything as a team and see what we can do in the race to progress.”

Franco Colapinto, 17th, 1:33.327

“It's been a tricky afternoon and of course we are all disappointed not to have gone through to at least Q2 in Qualifying. We were simply not as quick in the wet as we have been in the dry. We were lacking grip and overall pace in the conditions whereas others did not seem to have as much difficulty. We have a lot to review and hopefully, if the conditions are similar tomorrow, we can extract more pace on the Intermediates compared to the Extreme Wets. Understanding today's result is one thing but we also have to be prepared for the race and give it our all. It will be a long race, there are some drivers out of position to normal as a result of grid penalties, so we'll need to grab all the opportunities which might come our way.”

Steve Nielsen, Managing Director

“It's been a very disappointing day with both cars out in Q1. We have some work to do to fully understand why we were one of the slowest cars in the wet in that session. From a strategy point of view, we had good track position and we were one of the last cars to the cross the line, which is just where you want to be with the track improving significantly lap after lap. So, to be that far off with all those considerations, and not looking competitive at all, is particularly puzzling for us. We will keep an eye on the forecast as it remains likely that the conditions will be similar tomorrow with more rain expected. We'll aim to find some solutions and give the drivers the tools they need to fight their way back up the field.”

Cadillac

Bottas was the first out at the start of the drenched Q1 segment, and slid his way around the track in what appeared to be very hairy conditions. Both cars managed to keep their sessions clean, but neither had the pace in the wet to advance. Bottas was the pick of the duo, with Perez dropping a place as he is due to start from the back thanks to taking on a raft of new PU components.

Sergio Perez, 21st, 1:34.509

“The track conditions were tricky, but I think starting a little earlier was definitely the right call. Overall, there were a few complaints here and there, but we made good progress and felt competitive today, which was a positive sign. I was confident going into my final lap, thinking it was going to be the one, but I think I cooled the tyres down a little too much and didn’t get enough temperature into them. That was a bit unfortunate, as I feel we could have achieved a much better result. Hopefully, we’ll get some rain and see how things develop from there.”

Valtteri Bottas, 20th, 1:33.774

“Some very tricky conditions today. The first two laps were more survival than qualifying, but I managed to keep it on track, and the pace looked quite promising in the early stages. We were able to get the tyres working quite quickly, but then towards the end, we started overheating the rear tyres and dropped to the back sadly. It was nice to have wet qualifying, with every other qualifying this year being dry - it always brings opportunities. Let's see what tomorrow brings for the race, as the forecast can be very unpredictable here, so we’re hoping for some action and to make the most of any opportunities that come our way.”

Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal

“An eventful day with dramatic weather conditions as we so often see here at Interlagos. During a dry FP3, we had a smooth session after electing to take a new ICE, turbo and MGUK on Checo’s car following the issue in Mexico, and both drivers completed their run plans. Qualifying was a significant challenge operationally, and huge credit to the team in the garage and on the pitwall for responding well to the shifting conditions. Both our drivers also demonstrated their wealth of experience, putting in solid laps and keeping the car on the tarmac where others struggled with the wet conditions and got caught out. We had a shot at getting through to Q2 today, but ultimately we didn’t manage to put everything together at the very end of the session when it mattered. Thank you to the fans who persevered through the delays and ultimately saw some great on-track action. We’ll regroup tonight and prepare for another unpredictable day tomorrow, with more rain forecast ahead of the race.”

Pirelli

Dario Marrafuschi, Pirelli Motorsport Director

"Today’s qualifying session provided a clear demonstration of wet-weather racing, with the cars able to exploit the Full Wet tyre during the opening phase when track conditions remained particularly challenging. The extreme wet tyre enabled running to resume after the delay, confirming its effectiveness even in the most demanding conditions and allowing the drivers to maintain a strong level of performance.

"Equally significant was the switch to Intermediates at the start of the second session. Thanks to the development work carried out over recent years on the crossover window, the Full Wet was able to remain effective even once standing water had disappeared from the circuit, making the subsequent transition to Intermediates particularly smooth as track conditions continued to improve.

"Current forecasts indicate a 60% chance of rain for tomorrow’s race, meaning a scenario similar to today’s cannot be ruled out should the Grand Prix take place wholly or partly on a wet track. In dry conditions, however, the most meaningful indications come from Friday’s second free practice session, the only one that provided representative long-run data.

"Analysis of the long runs has led us to revise the simulations carried out before the weekend. Wear proved higher than expected, resulting in greater performance loss over the course of a stint. For this reason, a two-stop strategy emerges as the preferred option, featuring two stints on Soft and one on Medium. This combination is estimated to offer an advantage of around three seconds over strategies involving all three available compounds. Using the Hard tyre alongside two Soft stints would result in a further increase in overall race time.

"The lower temperatures expected on Sunday, combined with the possibility of a track offering less grip than was seen on Friday, could further favour the softer compounds, which provide greater grip and come up to temperature more quickly. A one-stop strategy appears significantly less competitive, with an estimated race time around ten seconds slower than the optimum two-stop approach. In this context, the undercut could prove decisive, particularly for drivers switching to a softer compound, as they would be able to exploit the immediate gain in grip to make up track position."

title: Lawson concedes he 'didn't quite maximise' his Q3 effort
excerpt:
Liam Lawson believes he didn’t maximise what he could achieve in Saturday’s eventful wet-weather Qualifying in Sao Paulo despite looking forward to a lofty P3 start in Sunday’s Grand Prix.

The Racing Bulls driver impressed throughout the challenging session as intense rainfall initially led to a substantial delay, before the drivers eventually ventured onto the track in sodden conditions.

With opportunities available for everyone on the grid to do something special amid the challenging weather, as well as the fact that a number of front-running drivers were carrying grid penalties, Lawson capitalised throughout to eventually secure fifth place.

With George Russell and Charles Leclerc two of the drivers taking penalties – along with the likes of Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen who are starting at the back – Lawson’s starting position in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix was elevated to third. However, despite managing to keep his car on track and impressively handling the challenge of standing water and the spray, Lawson conceded he felt there was more to extract from his Q3 effort.

“Obviously, we're in a good place for tomorrow, but we didn't quite maximise it,” Lawson said.

“We had really good speed today, and I tried to make a gap before the last lap. I caught Fernando [Alonso] in the first one, then I aborted, and then it rained. So, I didn't really get to do that final lap. But obviously, we get lucky tomorrow with a couple of places.”

With the teams braced for potentially more disruptive weather during Sunday’s race at Interlagos, Lawson acknowledged that he felt Racing Bulls would have a better chance of scoring big if the treacherous conditions continued.

“I think we have more of a chance, probably, in the wet,” he added. “But there's also a big risk with that, and we have a quick car in the dry.”

The Kiwi has also been at the focus in one of the main talking points this weekend as Racing Bulls are yet to announce their driver line-up for 2027. With Lawson showing his talent at various points this season he was left to question what else he had to do to prove he was worthy of being kept in a seat next season when asked by the media about the situation on Thursday.

With this latest eye-catching performance in Qualifying, Lawson was also asked if an outing like that could help swing things in his favour.

“I mean, yeah, but it's been like this for months now,” he told F1 TV. “So, at this point, honestly, every time I get in the car, I'm just trying to enjoy it. And today I did.

“You know, there's a lot of horsepower in these cars, not much grip today. So, you're really, like, there are places where it's probably five seconds before you get to full throttle and it's different for us. So, yeah, at the moment, being in the car is the most enjoyable part, I'd say.”

Meanwhile it was a tale of reliability woe for Lawson’s Racing Bulls team mate Arvid Lindblad as the British rookie was told to stop the car during Q2 due to a power unit problem, bringing about a premature end to his session.

That meant he missed Q3 for only the third time in the last 13 Grands Prix, qualified in P14, and he will line up in P12 for the race with the various grid penalties applied. It was especially disappointing for him considering his performance in the first part of Qualifying and the eventual starting position for his team mate.

“Q1 was good,” he explained afterwards. “I felt really good, very happy. I mean, I wasn't able to do the last lap, but I think on the penultimate lap I was P3 or something.

"So, I mean, I was fast, I was feeling good, and then Q2, from the beginning, the car felt very strange. And then a PU (power unit) issue.”

title: Norris details how he excelled in wet Sao Paulo Qualifying
excerpt:
Lando Norris has explained how he made the difference during a rain-soaked Qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, in which he beat Mercedes’ George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

Poor visibility, low grip and less-than-ideal weather made for an exhilarating session that saw nine different teams make it through to Q3, but it was Norris who put it all together when it mattered to take top spot.

He posted a 1m 27.470s before the rain intensified and forced others to abandon their laps, marking Norris’ third consecutive pole at Interlagos and McLaren’s fourth of the 2026 season.

“I had good confidence in the car – that’s always a good start,” the Briton explained after the session. “You want a car you feel you can push on. Especially with how wet it was, every bit of confidence you can get is a good thing and rewards you heavily.

“Obviously through Qualifying you start to see the pack even out and the pecking order go back a little bit to who has a good package, who has the most confidence. But into Q3, it was a lot more about who could push the most and just make the least mistakes.

“You had two laps, two opportunities to put things together, get a good lap, get the tyres in a good window – but also to then not make a mistake, to brake later, to accelerate harder but not lock the tyre and not have wheelspin.

“In these conditions it’s so easy to make these little errors which can be costly. My lap was just very clean and, in the end, that’s what you want.

“I couldn’t have done any more today. It was just a very nice, clean lap in, no mistakes – that’s what I managed to do.”

With the potential of more rain for Sunday’s 71-lap Grand Prix, Norris also seemed optimistic that he can continue to avoid errors and hold off new World Champion Antonelli, who will start P2 after Russell’s five-place grid penalty is imposed.

He said: “If I want to win tomorrow, we need rain. I think in the dry conditions, we don’t quite have the speed of our competitors, so it’s nice that in the rain I feel like I can make a bit more of a difference.

“I make up for a little bit of the lack of speed we have compared to them. I need it to stay raining all night.

“Obviously I want a good race, so I don’t mind a little bit of rain through the whole session. With Kimi behind, who’s probably the quickest this weekend, it’s going to be a tough challenge.”

McLaren endured contrasting fortunes at Interlagos as Oscar Piastri was eliminated in Q2 for the second consecutive weekend, trailing in P12 after he was hindered by a late red flag for Rafael Camara’s crash.

With only a short amount of time left on the clock, it was confirmed that the segment wouldn’t be resumed, although the Australian may be slightly comforted by the fact that grid penalties for others will promote him to P10.

“Definitely at the beginning of the session, it was tough,” Piastri said. “I think towards the end it was definitely getting easier, but you needed a couple of laps to get temperature into the inters.

“It was very, very challenging. We’ll try and make our way forward tomorrow. I think [the order] could be pretty jumbled. There are obviously a few grid penalties around so we’ll have to wait and see what it’s like.”

title: 'First Q3 of the season feels good' in Brazil – Alonso
excerpt:
Fernando Alonso admits that "the first Q3 of the season feels good", as the Aston Martin driver finished ninth quickest in a wet Qualifying ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

The two-time World Champion enjoyed his best Saturday of the season at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, during a session which was initially delayed due to heavy rain.

Once proceedings resumed, Alonso circulated in the top half of the field, finishing P8, P7 and P9 across the three Qualifying segments, with the best of the conditions coming at the very start in Q3.

"Not fun because the conditions were tricky. The level of focus was quite high today," said Alonso when asked about the session.

"Unknown conditions for everyone, especially on this year's car. I think we didn't have much practice on the wets. It was all experimental a little bit and the first Q3 of the season feels good."

Aston Martin have endured a difficult season under the new-for-2026 regulations, and although a revised car mid-season has helped to improve performance, Honda's power unit is still lacking power and reliability.

Alonso has scored the team's only points this year, with top-10 finishes in Monaco, the Netherlands and Malaysia.

The Spaniard, who will start P8 due to a grid penalty for Charles Leclerc, believes that more points could be possible in Sunday's 71-lap race, but only if wet weather appears.

"It opens a new possibility for us. Obviously the conditions, let's see if tomorrow is wet all through the race, maybe we have a chance to score points," said Alonso.

"If not, I think we will go back to our natural position. FP3 in the dry was a little bit disappointing, so we need to remain with the feet on the ground."

title: Verstappen sets out goal from back of the grid in Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Max Verstappen is targeting a fun outing at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as he attempts to work his way forwards from the back of the grid, with Red Bull opting to serve an engine penalty at Interlagos.

It was confirmed prior to Qualifying that Verstappen had amassed 30 places worth of penalties due to going beyond his season allocation for the Internal Combustion Engine (ICE), Turbo Charger and Exhaust, meaning that he joins the likes of both Ferrari drivers and Mercedes’ George Russell in taking penalties this weekend.

When it came to Saturday’s session, Verstappen participated in Q1 and, despite progressing to Q2, did not run in that segment, meaning that he wound up P16. His penalties, however, drop him back to second-to-last place in P21.

The four-time World Champion managed the challenging conditions of the session – which was delayed in getting underway due to heavy rain – but conceded when speaking afterwards that the plan had been to simply record a lap.

“I know that I have to start from the back, so we don’t want to take too much risk and [we] just put a lap on the board in Q1,” Verstappen explained. “And yeah, that’s what we did.”

Verstappen famously enjoyed a stunning rise through the field during a rain-affected race in Sao Paulo back in 2024, with the Dutch racer climbing up the order to go from P17 to victory.

Quizzed on the thinking behind taking his penalty at Interlagos, Verstappen responded: “I mean, we saw an issue and we decided to take the penalty here.

“Maybe it’s the best place to take it, but who knows. We’ll see tomorrow how far we can move up to the front. [We’ll] try and have a bit of fun out there.”

title: Norris clinches pole in rain-affected Sao Paolo Qualifying
excerpt:
Lando Norris came out on top in a test of bravery at the rain-soaked Interlagos circuit, with the McLaren driver securing pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after severe delays to the session.

The Brazilian weather once again made for an exhilarating Qualifying as drivers took on the challenge of a wet track, and Norris posted a 1m 27.470s to deny Mercedes’ George Russell and Kimi Antonelli top spot.

Russell will be demoted following a five-place grid penalty, but qualified ahead of his team mate, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc – who will also lose 10 positions for Sunday’s race – and Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson.

Nico Hulkenberg was a magnificent sixth for Audi as the conditions created chances for the midfield, with Isack Hadjar slotting into seventh. Haas’ Ollie Bearman, Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Williams’ Alex Albon rounded out the top 10 in some of the greatest Qualifying performances of the season for their respective teams.

Further incoming penalties for Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen will see them tumble to the back of the grid, so neither was too stressed about being eliminated in Q2 – indeed, the Dutchman didn’t participate at all.

Behind the 11th-placed Ferrari driver, Oscar Piastri suffered his second consecutive Q2 exit as a late red flag for Rafael Camara’s crash prevented him from improving and left the Brazilian rookie in P13.

An order to stop the car also resigned Arvid Lindblad to P14 – he led Williams’ Carlos Sainz and the penalised Verstappen as the final drivers who failed to progress to Q3.

Earlier in Qualifying, a breathless opening segment saw Alpine’s Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly knocked out as they crossed the line in tandem, leaving them in P17 and P18 ahead of Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll.

Cadillac failed to capitalise on the challenging weather as Valtteri Bottas settled for P20 in front of his team mate Sergio Perez, whilst Gabriel Bortoleto wound up last on the times after hitting the wall in Q1.

AS IT HAPPENED

Q1 – Norris quickest in thrilling wet start to Qualifying

The drivers had been treated to three dry practice sessions – which saw Norris, Antonelli and Verstappen top the times – but it felt inevitable that the unpredictable weather Interlagos is known for would arrive at some point, and it did so in the build-up to Qualifying.

Prior to the heavy rainfall, a number of grid penalties had been confirmed for Sunday’s race – Russell would lose five places, Leclerc would drop 10 positions no matter where he qualified, and Hamilton would join Verstappen and Perez at the back of the grid.

With four leading drivers ruled out of contention for the front rows, that opened up a fantastic opportunity for those in the midfield to fight for better Qualifying results, although the risk of rain was still very much in place.

In fact, it increased dramatically as the session began and the red flag was waved just under three minutes in, with Antonelli and Hadjar complaining that their race suits were soaked from their short trips onto the track.

After a significant delay, Q1 resumed once the weather stabilised and the racers ventured back out on full wet tyres, producing some understandably cautious reconnaissance laps around what was still a very damp circuit.

The first timed efforts were completed by the Cadillac pair as they sent up massive amounts of spray whilst circulating, but it didn't take long for Verstappen to shoot to the top with a 1m 37.932s. In an incredible sign of the difference a driver could make in the conditions, Alonso was the next to set the fastest time before the Dutchman found even more to reclaim the position.

While others were struggling to adapt much more – Camara briefly spun and Bortoleto nearly got stuck in the grass – the times continued to rapidly improve as Hulkenberg, Hamilton, Russell and Bearman all took a turn at seizing P1.

Everyone was right on the edge as Russell posted a 1m 32.441s, and with the constant threat of another interruption, it was tricky to predict who would escape the drop zone. With two minutes to go, Perez, Sainz, Stroll, Bottas, Colapinto and Bortoleto occupied the bottom six positions.

McLaren’s Norris ended at the top of the timesheets with a 1m 30.939s, but the Alpine duo of Colapinto and Gasly were eliminated alongside Stroll, Bottas, Perez, Bortoleto – the latter having failed to find the time he needed after slamming into the barrier.

Knocked out: Colapinto, Gasly, Stroll, Bottas, Perez, Bortoleto

Q2 – Nine teams finish in the top 10 as Camara crashes

The second stage of Qualifying would only see 15 drivers take part as Verstappen decided to call it a day in anticipation of his hefty grid penalty, making Hadjar the sole Red Bull in the session.

As the drivers finished their opening laps, Norris surged into first place again and claimed that it wouldn’t be long until they could switch to intermediates, confirming the expectation that conditions would only continue to get better.

He was soon displaced by Leclerc, who broke into the 1m 29s bracket to lead the McLaren man, Antonelli, Lawson and Russell in the top five. Haas debutant Camara couldn’t quite reach their heights, but did enough to linger at the edge of the elimination zone following his Q1 spin.

Things weren’t looking as good for Racing Bulls’ Lindblad as he was instructed to stop the car at Turn 5, bringing a premature end to his session. Meanwhile, his team mate Lawson seemed comfortable in seventh place, but the order had potential to drastically change with drivers making the move to intermediate tyres.

That decision brought immediate gains for the New Zealander that sent him into P1, 1.6s clear of Bearman, and was followed by another improvement for Russell. It looked like more quick laps were to come for others before Camara drove straight into the barrier to bring out the red flag with less than a minute remaining.

The session was therefore stopped for a second time and left Hamilton – who will drop to the back of the grid with his aforementioned penalty for a new power unit – Piastri, Camara, Lindblad, Sainz and Verstappen as the eliminated drivers.

Knocked out: Hamilton, Piastri, Camara, Lindblad, Sainz, Verstappen

Q3 – Norris storms to pole as midfield teams celebrate stellar results

Following a short delay, Q3 kicked off under darkening skies at Interlagos, and the attention wasn’t just on the battle for pole position, but also what the surviving midfield drivers – namely Lawson, Bearman, Hulkenberg, Albon and Alonso – could achieve.

Warnings of intense rain meant that the early laps could be crucial, so Alonso ensured he was the first driver on track and executed a 1m 30.311s on the intermediate tyres before Lawson went significantly faster for Racing Bulls.

While efforts from Norris and Russell took them to the top, newly-crowned World Champion Antonelli could only manage fourth behind Lawson, with the McLaren driver going on to snatch provisional pole.

As the rain grew heavier, it was evident that the best track conditions had passed with seven minutes still on the clock. That created immense frustration for Russell, who fumed at his team for telling him to abandon his lap as he slotted into second behind polesitter Norris.

Antonelli ultimately finished third ahead of Leclerc, Lawson and Audi's Hulkenberg. Close behind, Hadjar qualified seventh for Red Bull, leaving Bearman, Alonso and Albon to complete the top 10 and mark a memorable day for their teams.

Key quote

"It's been a long day," Norris said. "It's been a great Qualifying. Obviously, to be on pole again here, it's different conditions to last year but I'm very happy. It's not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it's going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning and not making any mistakes, and that's exactly what we did, so it's been a very good day."

Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen are to start the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 20th and 21st, respectively, after major engine penalties.

title: Liam Lawson takes blame for key error despite equaling F1 career-best
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has taken the blame for a key error in Q3 at a treacherous Sao Paulo GP qualifying, which he feels cost him a shot at a career-best result.

Lawson qualified in fifth place on the road at Interlagos in the heavily delayed qualifying ahead of the race, but will be promoted to third place after George Russell and Charles Leclerc take grid penalties from second and fourth, respectively.

It equals Lawson's career-best grid spot, which was third at the 2025 Azerbaijan GP, but the New Zealander described how in Q3, he got too close to the Aston Martin of Fernando Alonso, which caused him to catch the two-time champion in the dreadfully wet conditions - and have to back off.

"I think we had a good chance, and we had a very strong car, so we were very good at the call to go to inters in Q2," Lawson began to media, including RacingNews365.

"That's what probably put us up there initially, but in Q3, I think we had a good chance at fighting the front guys, but I just did not make a big enough gap. It is my fault.

"These cars have a lot of horsepower and not much grip, and so you are sliding around, and it is a shame, as I made a gap to Fernando, but I caught him too much on the first lap.

"Then I had to abort the last lap, which probably ended up being the optimal one, and then it rained.

"But we get a couple of places [due to the penalties], so we start in a good place. I didn't qualify third; I qualified fifth, so it is still a good place to start, and I'll take the two positions, but you always want to maximise as a driver."

[Article continues below]

Lawson looks ahead to Sao Paulo GP

Looking ahead to the race, Lawson predicted that if conditions were similar to qualifying, it would be a chaotic race with "red flags."

"It is going to be interesting. When it rains, the problem is that it rains so heavily that you can't really drive," he added.

"There was a period in qualifying when we got quite lucky, where it was just consistent, but if it was like the rain before qualifying, then you can't really race.

"So if it rains out there [in the race], there'll be some red flags.

"When we started, it was extremely sketchy, and we were definitely pushing it.

"I like the fact that we were out there and not in the garage, and it was risky, but there wasn't an accident. But at the start, it was definitely borderline, as there was a lot of aquaplaning."

title: Lewis Hamilton reveals details of Charles Leclerc meeting after Ferrari tension
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has revealed that he and Charles Leclerc have "squashed" the simmering tension that had built up between the Ferrari teammates following last Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.

The two drivers clashed on the opening lap at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez when Leclerc attempted an outside move on his teammate at Turn 4, sending both cars off the circuit before Leclerc rejoined ahead of Hamilton across the grass.

The incident cost Ferrari dearly as Max Verstappen slipped past Hamilton into second, and then netted the lead, and the win, after Leclerc was later handed a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage.

It was the latest flashpoint in a season that has already produced friction between the two drivers, following a strategy disagreement at Zandvoort and a first-lap coming-together at Monza.

Team principal Fred Vasseur said afterwards that the accumulation of such moments reflected two highly competitive teammates repeatedly fighting each other on track, and that individual battles had started to compromise the wider interests of the team.

Vasseur is understood to have held debriefs with both drivers following the Mexico incident, but Hamilton made clear it was a separate conversation, directly with Leclerc, that resolved matters, speaking ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix weekend.

Asked if things were now on a good footing between himself and his teammate, speaking to Sky Sports F1, Hamilton said: "Fred hasn't cleared the air. It was me and Charles. We sat and spoke, we squashed it, and we're moving on.

"We still have a huge amount of respect for each other. I'm glad we had a chat, and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine, as normal. Sometimes in those certain scenarios, it just takes having a conversation.

"There's been no demands from either side. It's just been both of us giving our points in areas we can do better and support each other. I'm hoping to have better races moving forward."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton - Qualifying was a practice session

Hamilton's comments come amid ongoing debate over whether Ferrari needs to introduce clearer rules of engagement for its two drivers, something Vasseur has so far resisted in favour of relying on mutual respect and post-race mediation.

The seven-time F1 champion then reflected on a tricky qualifying session at Interlagos, where torrential rain dominated.

The situation was further complicated for Hamilton by the fact that after taking on a new internal combustion engine ahead of final practice, that system then encountered issues, leading to a complete PU change going into qualifying.

After setting the 11th fastest time, albeit because there was no need to push because of the penalties, and knowing he will start at the back of the grid, Hamilton said: "I love qualifying, and getting to drive in the rain; it's such an amazing track to race in all conditions, but in the wet particularly.

"I wish I could have stayed out and had a bit of a battle with everyone, but we had that problem in P3. We didn't get in many laps there, so it was basically a practice session for me to try and figure out what it feels like in these conditions, just in case tomorrow it's raining."

Leclerc will start the race from 14th due to serving a 10-place penalty of his own after taking on a new ICE.

title: Max Verstappen shares chaotic Sao Paulo GP wish as huge F1 penalty looms
excerpt:
Max Verstappen shares chaotic Sao Paulo GP wish as huge F1 penalty looms

Max Verstappen has named his desire to see the Sao Paulo Grand Prix feature a lot of safety cars to bring him back into contention.

The Red Bull driver will be starting from the back of the grid at Interlagos, with Lewis Hamilton, after his team elected to fit a new power unit to his RB22 machine after an issue on Friday.

In the wet qualifying session in Brazil, Verstappen completed Q1, and looked competitive before opting to save tyres in Q2 by not running, with the race forecast to be as wet as qualifying.

Reflecting on his day and looking ahead to the race, Verstappen expressed a desire for a chaotic grand prix which could bring him back into contention for a strong result as he looks to consolidate second place in the drivers' standings - where he leads Hamilton, who is also taking an engine penalty, by two points.

When asked what his desire for the grand prix was, with the conditions expected to be similar to qualifying, Verstappen indicated a chaotic wish.

"Lots of safety cars, so they can't pull away," he told media, including RacingNews365.

"Then they can keep coming back to me, but I don't really think too much about it, so I'll just go from Lap 1 and see where I end up."

As for coming through the field with Hamilton, Verstappen added that he hoped "we can clear the cars in front as quickly as we can."

Reflecting on the call to box at the end of Q1 and not partake in Q2, Verstappen agreed it was the "right call."

"I wasn't fighting for anything; my mind is already set to [the race]," he said.

"So it was just about doing a lap, not risking anything, but every lap I did, we were up there, but for me, that is not a surprise."

title: George Russell fury after Mercedes call wrecks Sao Paulo GP pole bid
excerpt:
George Russell has aired his frustration as Mercedes' call to abort his Q3 lap in Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying he felt was good enough for pole.

The Briton ultimately took second on the grid in Sao Paulo after a lengthy rain delay of around 90 minutes, with Lando Norris sailing to a fourth pole of the season.

Russell was 0.204s behind his fellow Briton Norris at the end, having been told by engineer Marcus Dudley to abort a lap after coming across the Williams of Alex Albon in the middle sector.

Russell felt this lap was good enough for pole position, with incoming rain then stopping drivers from making any further improvements, with Russell set to drop to seventh after a five-place penalty is applied for a new ICE engine component.

Over the radio, Russell expressed his frustration, with Toto Wolff intervening.

Russell: Mate, you fu**ing told me to back off! What the hell?

Wolff: George, you're P2.

Russell: P2? I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1.

Wolff: I know. I know.

Reflecting after stepping out of the car, Russell felt he should have just finished the lap he was on.

"That was definitely the pole lap, so [aborting] is a misjudgment on our side," Russell explained.

"I need to understand what happened, and the rain was coming, and we should have just finished the lap."

When then asked what was possible in the race from seventh, Russell explained his confidence in the W17 machine was growing in the wet.

"It depends on the weather, but I felt good out there," he said.

"It is the first time in a while I've felt confident in the car, and I felt more confident in the wet than I do in the dry. I don't really understand why that was.

"I felt more like myself, in the fight for pole every single lap, but unfortunately when it mattered, we didn't execute."

title: Lando Norris scores Sao Paulo GP hat-trick: 'I figured it out pretty quickly'
excerpt:
Lando Norris felt he managed to "figure out pretty quick" how to drive in the rain after qualifying for the São Paulo Grand Prix was dominated by torrential conditions.

Q1 at a sodden Interlagos was red-flagged after just two and a half minutes, following which there followed an 82-minute delay as FIA race control waited for the conditions to ease.

When they did, Norris was superb, ultimately finishing top of the timesheet when it mattered most, beating George Russell in his Mercedes to top spot on the grid, with incoming champion Kimi Antonelli third quickest.

Antonelli will start on the front row alongside Norris due to Russell serving a five-place penalty for his W17 taking on a new internal combustion engine.

After claiming a third successive pole position for the São Paulo event, speaking to Sky Sports F1, Norris said: "Well, it's been a long day; it's been a great qualifying.

"Obviously, to be on pole again here two years in a row [sic] is...different conditions to last year, but I'm very happy.

"It wasn't easy conditions out there, especially when you know it's going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that's exactly what we did, so it's been a very good day.

As to whether he had learned anything given the lack of wet running this season with the new power units, Norris said: "Well, this was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quickly.

"It was tough - wet, inters, all different tyres. It was very windy as well on the last couple of laps, so it's certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow.

"These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick, so [I'm] just happy. Today was about getting on pole; it doesn't really matter how you do it. So very pleased with that."

Huge delay to Q1 but qualifying starts

title: Rafael Camara sparks second qualifying red flag after home Sao Paulo crash
excerpt:
Rafael Camara blotted his F1 debut by crashing in the second qualifying session ahead of his home grand prix in São Paulo.

Camara, who will replace the axed Esteban Ocon at Haas on a permanent basis next season, was given his opportunity by the team for the race at Interlagos.

Haas drafted in Ryo Hirakawa over the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend after team principal Ayao Komatsu decided the Frenchman would not continue following Friday's practice session.

Hurtling across the grass, Camara hit the brakes and in the sodden conditions was a passenger as he buried the nose of his car into a barrier bringing out the red flags.

In Q1, fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto also went off at Junçao, spinning sideways into the same barrier hit by Camara, damaging the rear wing on his Audi, leading to him retiring after making his way back to the garage.
